R2.why: The INK & IRON title block is the largest element and leads, the bordered first-run card 'CAN YOU READ THIS COMFORTABLY?' sits centred over the painting, with the campaign column and status line beside and below.

R5.why: The greyed campaign buttons each carry the tooltip 'Waiting for the game's server…' and the red status line says why; the live buttons answer and the slider is a real control the card tells you to drag.

R8.why: The card names its action ('Drag the slider…') and offers 'Looks right' and 'Size for this screen'; the campaign buttons are visible beneath.

main_menu.R4_note: At 5120 the first-run card's slider reads 140% while its 1920 twin reads 100%, and the card's text is smaller than the menu column beside it.

R2.why: The bordered SETTINGS panel is centred in the frame with no card over it, DISPLAY and INTERFACE leading; the eye goes to it over the dimmed menu column.

R5.why: Drop-downs, buttons, the High contrast toggle and Back all look like controls and answer; the disabled Connect / Disconnect and campaign buttons each carry their reason in a tooltip.

R8.why: Each setting is a labelled control with a hint, and Back is a full-width button.

main_menu_settings.R4_note: SOUND, SMARTER PARSING, SPOKEN ORDERS, CONTROLS and CREDITS are below the inner scroll; only a thin scrollbar says they exist.

R2.why: The CAMPAIGN MENU panel dominates the dimmed war room and its Settings block, with the Interface Scale slider, is unfolded at full panel width, not squeezed.

R5.why: All buttons and drop-downs look like controls and are in the record; the disabled Connect / Disconnect give their reasons in tooltips.

R8.why: The slider and its two buttons are visible, and Main Menu / Quit are labelled.

war_room_pause_settings.R4_note: The sound rows are below the inner scroll, and there is no Resume or close control on the panel; the way back to the game is only the Esc key.
